        - heading "Understand Graph Colouring" [level=2]
        - paragraph: "A proper vertex colouring assigns colours to vertices so adjacent vertices always receive different colours. A useful rule is Edge constraint: uv in E => c(u) != c(v). You can learn Graph Colouring by trying one small example instead of long theory."

      - article:
        - heading "3. UNDERSTAND THE RULE" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Key definition and rule.
        - text: Definition (Proper Vertex Colouring)
        - paragraph: A colouring of a graph G = (V, E) is proper if u and v have different colours for every edge uv ∈ E.
        - text: Key rule
        - paragraph: The chromatic number χ(G) is the minimum number of colours needed for a proper vertex colouring of G.
        - text: Quick facts
        - paragraph: • χ(G) ≥ 1 for any graph G.
        - paragraph: • If G has a triangle, then χ(G) ≥ 3.
        - paragraph: • χ(Kₙ) = n (complete graph on n vertices).
